Mot. to Dismiss at 12-13. Ex. A § 9.1 (emphasis added). 19	The dispute resolution clause in the 2004 Agreement contains two clauses, one of which is mandatory (the parties shall refer the matter to senior executives to attempt to negotiate a resolution) and the other which is permissive (the parties may refer the matter to nonbinding mediation). 20	L.P. and S.A., who are not parties to the 2004 Agreement, also contend that the dispute resolution clause requires their dismissal from this action. See United States v. Benish, 5 F.3d 20, 26 (3d Cir.1993) (rejecting a party’s claim where the party “provided] no legal support for his argument or any persuasive reason” for the court to find in his favor). The Court sees no persuasive reason to dismiss Skold’s entire Complaint based on this unsupported argument. See, e.g., LBL Skysystems (USA), Inc. v. APG-Am., Inc., No. 02-5379, 2005 WL 2140240, at *30 (E.D.Pa. Aug. 31, 2005) (holding that a “party that engages in discovery and files pretrial motions waives a contract’s alternative dispute resolution provision”); Smith v. IMG Worldwide, Inc., 360 F.Supp.2d 681, 687 (E.D.Pa.2005) (finding that a party’s engaging in motion practice and providing “substantial discovery” constituted waiver of contractual alternative dispute resolution provision).
22	Viewing the four years’ worth of docket entries in the TTAB action, the Court considers that Inc. did not file a motion to stay the TTAB proceedings pending executive-level negotiations and instead filed, inter alia, motions to dismiss, a protective order, multiple summary judgment motions (one of which was partially granted in its favor), and a final brief in preparation for trial. See also generally Registrant’s Trial Brief, Sköld v. Galderma Labs., Inc., Cancellation No. 92052897 (T.T.A.B. Aug. 13, 2014), Docket No. 81. This four-year history of litigation in the cancellation action — from filing nearly through trial — is, on its face, inconsistent with the notion that Inc. was willing to engage in the good-faith executive-level negotiations required by the dispute resolution provision.
23	Moreover, the Court can look to the TTAB’s grant of partial summary judgment in favor of Inc. and dismissing Skold’s abandonment claim as a concrete example of an instance where Inc.’s conduct inconsistent with the dispute resolution clause caused prejudice to Skold, not to mention the expenditure of time, cost, and resources attendant to maintaining a multi-year trademark cancellation action. 12	International ACH and Wire Transactions If your Account receives incoming ACH transactions (either credits or debits) or wire transfers initiated from outside of the United States, both you and we are subject to the Operating Rules and Guidelines of the National Automated Clearing House Association (“NACHA”) or the rules of any wire transfer system involved, and the laws enforced by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (“OFAC”). {"clause_id":"c171","reasoning_cat1":"An extremely long sum-and-subtract definition with a mislabelled '(4)' for '(i)' and a deeply nested parenthetical about upfront payments under replacement swaps whose grammar is hard to follow.","reasoning_cat2":"It attributes repurchase obligations to the Sponsor, Saxon, the Majority Class CE Certificateholder and the Originator 'pursuant to Sections 2.02 and 2.03', but Section 2.03 is captioned as the Master Servicer's own representations, so the cross-reference sits awkwardly with the section it names.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.31},

{"clause_id":"c175","reasoning_cat1":"'or other realization as provided by applicable law' is a catch-all following two specific methods, and the reach of that catch-all is genuinely open.","reasoning_cat2":"Depends on the Final Recovery Determination definition, which itself rests on the Servicer's judgment; consistent in structure.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.09},

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c181","reasoning_cat1":"'a majority or greater Percentage Interest' is a redundant but definite threshold.","reasoning_cat2":"This Holder is given purchase and repurchase rights in Sections 4.21 and 11.01 and appears in the Interest Funds and Principal Funds definitions; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c182","reasoning_cat1":"A dense weighted-average rate with nested caps and a proviso; the exclusion list differs between the opening words (AA, IO and P) and the cap carve-outs (ZZ), which takes care to follow.","reasoning_cat2":"It interlocks with the Class CE Pass-Through Rate and REMIC II Regular Interest ZZ Maximum Interest Deferral Amount definitions, which use parallel cap language; no conflict found.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c183","reasoning_cat1":"Party definition; nothing to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Preamble and the Securities Administrator definition.","prob_cat1":0.02,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c184","reasoning_cat1":"Pure cross-reference; no independent content.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 4.18(b) supplies the meaning; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c185","reasoning_cat1":"Definite two-element definition.","reasoning_cat2":"It duplicates the float-earnings element already built into the Master Servicing Fee definition, so the same amount appears to be counted in both definitions.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c186","reasoning_cat1":"A per-loan fee formula which then tacks on 'and any amounts earned on permitted investments in the Distribution Account during the Master Servicer Float Period' — a pool-level item bolted onto a per-loan calculation.","reasoning_cat2":"The same float amount is separately included in Master Servicing Compensation, creating an apparent double count between the two definitions and Section 4.14.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c187","reasoning_cat1":"A single number; nothing to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Net Mortgage Rate and Mortgage Loan Schedule definitions.","prob_cat1":0.02,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c188","reasoning_cat1":"A precisely bounded one-day period; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Master Servicing Fee and Master Servicing Compensation definitions.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c189","reasoning_cat1":"Definite; taken from the Mortgage Note.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Periodic Rate Cap and Mortgage Loan Schedule definitions.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c190","reasoning_cat1":"The amount is whatever the Depositor calculates 'in accordance with the EMC's internal risk management process in respect of similar instruments' — an unascertainable, wholly discretionary and externally located standard, and the closing clause repeats itself.","reasoning_cat2":"No other provision of this Agreement defines or constrains EMC's internal process, so the term has no anchor anywhere in the instrument.","prob_cat1":0.44,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c191","reasoning_cat1":"Naming definition; nothing to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the MERS System, MIN and MOM Loan definitions.","prob_cat1":0.02,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c192","reasoning_cat1":"One-line definition; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 2.01's MERS assignment mechanics.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c193","reasoning_cat1":"One-line definition; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the MOM Loan definition and the Mortgage Loan Schedule item (x).","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c194","reasoning_cat1":"Definite; taken from the Mortgage Note.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Maximum Mortgage Rate and Periodic Rate Cap definitions.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c195","reasoning_cat1":"The definition defines a loan type by describing MERS's role rather than the loan, so grammatically 'MOM Loan' is defined as 'MERS acting as the mortgagee' — a drafting slip.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 2.01 uses MOM Loan as a category of Mortgage Loan, which is what the definition plainly intends; the mismatch is formal only.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c196","reasoning_cat1":"Pure cross-reference; no independent content.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 6.06 supplies the meaning; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c197","reasoning_cat1":"Naming definition; nothing to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Rating Agency definition.","prob_cat1":0.02,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c198","reasoning_cat1":"Defines Mortgage as an instrument creating a 'first lien', yet the Agreement elsewhere expressly contemplates second lien Mortgage Loans.","reasoning_cat2":"The Mortgage Loan Schedule definition provides for 'each second lien Mortgage Loan' and a CLTV, which cannot be reconciled with a Mortgage that must create a first lien.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.40},
{"clause_id":"c199","reasoning_cat1":"Definite; contents are fixed by the Section 2.01 list plus later additions.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 2.01, 2.02 and 4.07/4.12 concerning custody and release of Mortgage Files.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c200","reasoning_cat1":"The deeming sentence turns on 'a breach of the representation contained in Section 2.03(b)(v) hereof', but Section 2.03(b) is a one-sentence survival clause with no subclauses, so the cited representation does not exist.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 2.03 is captioned as the Master Servicer's and Securities Administrator's own corporate representations, so a defined term that makes loan status depend on Section 2.03(b)(v) cannot be reconciled with Article II as drafted.","prob_cat1":0.34,"prob_cat2":0.47},
{"clause_id":"c201","reasoning_cat1":"Definite; names parties, date and form exhibit.","reasoning_cat2":"Central to Sections 2.02(c) and 2.02(d), which make the MLPA the source of repurchase obligations; consistent in itself.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c202","reasoning_cat1":"A cross-reference definition, but the term is confusingly close to the separately defined 'Purchase Price' and 'Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement'.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 11.01 supplies the calculation; the overlap with the Purchase Price definition (which covers repurchases under Sections 2.02 and 4.21) is a possible source of confusion but not a conflict.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.15},
{"clause_id":"c203","reasoning_cat1":"The schedule specification contains several plain mechanical defects: two separate items lettered '(aa)', a garbled '(¢4)', 'the the Periodic Rate Cap', 'acode indicating whether the Mortgage Loan is has a balloon payment', four '[reserved]' items, and reliance on 'CLTV' and 'Monthly Payment', neither of which is a defined term.","reasoning_cat2":"The Schedule is the instrument that identifies the Mortgage Loans for the Mortgage Loans, Originator and Seller definitions and for Section 2.02's certification against Exhibit B, so its internal defects propagate into the conveyance and acceptance machinery.","prob_cat1":0.55,"prob_cat2":0.38},
{"clause_id":"c204","reasoning_cat1":"'or other evidence of indebtedness' is a mild catch-all but the referent is plain.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 2.01's delivery requirements and the lost-note affidavit proviso.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c205","reasoning_cat1":"One line; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Net Mortgage Rate and Adjustable Rate Mortgage Loan definitions.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c206","reasoning_cat1":"One line; definite though very general.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Mortgage and REO Property definitions.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c207","reasoning_cat1":"One line; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Mortgage Note definition.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c208","reasoning_cat1":"Definite arithmetic subtraction of three specified rates.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Servicing Fee Rate, Master Servicing Fee Rate and LPMI Fee definitions and the Net Rate Cap.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c209","reasoning_cat1":"Two quite different caps are given the same defined name — one for the Certificates and a different weighted-average formula 'for federal income tax purposes' — and the swap deduction is expressed as a rate divided by a balance multiplied by 12 with an actual/360 adjustment bolted on afterwards.","reasoning_cat2":"The Marker Rate and REMIC II Regular Interest ZZ definitions both invoke 'the Net Rate Cap for the REMIC III Regular Interest', so which of the two Net Rate Caps applies where is a live question across several provisions.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c210","reasoning_cat1":"Definite; expressly excludes Swap Termination Payments.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Swap Termination Payment definition and Section 4.22(c).","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c211","reasoning_cat1":"The determination rests entirely on the advancing party's own 'good faith judgment' of ultimate recoverability, an inherently contestable standard, and the catch-all 'or otherwise' has no boundary.","reasoning_cat2":"It interacts with Section 6.01's advancing obligation and with the Interest Funds/Principal Funds deductions, which allow reimbursement of Nonrecoverable Advances; consistent in structure.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c212","reasoning_cat1":"One defined term is given three different meanings in four sentences — a Class CE amount, a federal tax amount, and a swap notional from Exhibit M — without any signal as to which governs a given use.","reasoning_cat2":"Uses of 'Notional Amount' in the Current Interest and Pass-Through Rate definitions do not say which limb applies, so the reader must infer it from context.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c213","reasoning_cat1":"Closed list; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Book-Entry Certificates and Private Certificates definitions, which together account for all classes.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c214","reasoning_cat1":"The bracketed catch-all 'any other officer customarily performing functions similar to those performed by any of the above designated officers' is a general phrase appended to a specific list, and its reach is genuinely uncertain.","reasoning_cat2":"It runs alongside the Servicing Officer and Responsible Officer definitions, which use different signing standards for different parties; no direct conflict found.","prob_cat1":0.20,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c215","reasoning_cat1":"A carefully laid-out fallback waterfall with a 'manifest error' finality clause; each step is specified and the last sentence is merely confirmatory.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Reference Bank Rate, Interest Determination Date and LIBOR Certificates definitions.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c216","reasoning_cat1":"'reasonably acceptable to each addressee' is a soft standard, and the independence proviso is triggered only for four listed sections plus REMIC interpretation.","reasoning_cat2":"It names Sections 2.05, 8.05, 8.07 and 12.01 and refers to 'the Seller' in the singular where the Agreement elsewhere speaks of 'the Sellers'; the singular/plural drift runs through the instrument.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c217","reasoning_cat1":"Definite; keyed to Section 11.01.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Optional Termination Date definition and Section 11.01.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c218","reasoning_cat1":"Definite 5% clean-up threshold.","reasoning_cat2":"Every Class Pass-Through Rate steps up after this date, so the definition is load-bearing; it is consistent with those definitions and with Section 11.01.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c219","reasoning_cat1":"Definite in form, but it makes the identity of the Originator turn entirely on an entry in the Mortgage Loan Schedule.","reasoning_cat2":"The Originator bears repurchase obligations under Sections 2.02(c) and (d), so an error or omission in the Schedule column would determine who owes those obligations; the Schedule definition itself is defective in places.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c220","reasoning_cat1":"Naming definition; nothing to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"Used only in the Delinquent definition; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.02,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c221","reasoning_cat1":"An 'all except (a), (b)' construction; definite and exhaustive.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 7.02 and 7.03 on transfer, exchange and replacement of Certificates.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c222","reasoning_cat1":"Definite; three cumulative conditions.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Liquidated Loan, Stated Principal Balance and Prepayment Period definitions.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c223","reasoning_cat1":"Definite excess computation with a circularity guard for the Extra Principal Distribution Amount.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Overcollateralization Target Amount and Release Amount definitions and Section 6.04.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c224","reasoning_cat1":"A lesser-of with a deeming proviso; the proviso says 'the amount pursuant to clause (y)' where it plainly means clause (y)(i) minus (y)(ii), a small looseness.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Overcollateralization Amount and Target Amount definitions and the Excess Cashflow definition.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c225","reasoning_cat1":"A three-branch stepdown formula; long but each branch is specified, including the Trigger Event freeze.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Stepdown Date and Trigger Event definitions and the REMIC II Overcollateralization Target Amount.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c226","reasoning_cat1":"Deliberately expansive ('any other interest therein, whether direct or indirect, legal or beneficial') but that breadth is the point rather than an ambiguity.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Permitted Transferee definition and the residual transfer restrictions.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c227","reasoning_cat1":"The opening sentence excludes the Class CE Certificates yet lists 'the Class CE Pass-Through Rate' among the applicable rates, and the following sentence then says the Class CE Certificate has no Pass-Through Rate — the two statements sit uneasily together.","reasoning_cat2":"The Class CE Pass-Through Rate definition applies to the Class CE Interest rather than the Certificate, which resolves the tension but only by careful reading across definitions.","prob_cat1":0.20,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c228","reasoning_cat1":"One line; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Securities Administrator definition and Section 6.04.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c229","reasoning_cat1":"Two alternative measures joined by 'or' with no priority stated, plus the typo 'all Certificates of the such Class'.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Denomination definition, which supplies the second measure.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c230","reasoning_cat1":"Definite; the parenthetical clarifies the interaction with the Maximum and Minimum Mortgage Rates.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Maximum/Minimum Mortgage Rate and Adjustment Date definitions.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c231","reasoning_cat1":"A ten-item list closed by the catch-all '(x) such other investments ... acceptable to each Rating Agency', and a proviso that exempts 'investments in units of money market funds pursuant to clause (v) above' when money market funds are clause (viii), not clause (v) — a plain mis-citation inside the operative proviso.","reasoning_cat2":"The mis-cited clause cannot be reconciled with the list as drafted, and the investment restrictions interlock with the Eligible Account definition and the Article V account provisions.","prob_cat1":0.36,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c232","reasoning_cat1":"An extremely long tax-driven exclusion with three lettered limbs; dense but each element tracks Code and Treasury Regulation language.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Transferee Affidavit, Ownership Interest and Residual Certificates provisions.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c233","reasoning_cat1":"A standard enumerated definition ending in 'or government, or any agency or political subdivision thereof'; conventional.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent throughout; no conflict found.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c234","reasoning_cat1":"Defines a rate by reference to a description in an offering document that is not part of this Agreement, giving the term no content on the face of the instrument.","reasoning_cat2":"The Prospectus Supplement is defined but not incorporated as an operative document, so the assumption is imported from outside the four corners.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.21},
{"clause_id":"c235","reasoning_cat1":"Definite; three synonyms for the same charge, sourced from the Mortgage Note.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Prepayment Charge Waiver Amount and Class P Certificate definitions.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c236","reasoning_cat1":"Definite, but it depends on a pinpoint citation to Section 5.01(a).","reasoning_cat2":"Section 5.01 is the Master Servicer Account provision, which is a plausible home for waived prepayment charges, but this Agreement's pinpoint cross-references are unreliable in several places.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.15},
{"clause_id":"c237","reasoning_cat1":"The subtraction adds together 'the related Servicing Fee', 'the Master Servicing Fee Rate' and 'the LPMI Fee' — mixing a rate with two dollar amounts — and the opening words 'the amount received from and including the 16th day ... if any, by which' are grammatically broken.","reasoning_cat2":"The parallel Net Mortgage Rate definition subtracts three rates, showing that this definition should have used the Master Servicing Fee, so the two provisions do not line up.","prob_cat1":0.34,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c238","reasoning_cat1":"Definite 16th-to-15th period with a first-period special rule.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Due Period and Prepayment Interest Shortfall definitions.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c239","reasoning_cat1":"The tail — 'if any or any replacement policy therefor through the related Interest Accrual Period for such Class relating to a Distribution Date' — is ungrammatical and refers to 'such Class' when no class has been mentioned.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 4.11 obliges maintenance of these policies, and the garbled temporal limitation makes the duration of the defined coverage unclear against that section.","prob_cat1":0.33,"prob_cat2":0.20},

{"clause_id":"c309","reasoning_cat1":"A four-limb subtraction with different measuring periods for each limb; long but each is specified, and the final sentence gives a clean rule for Liquidated Loans.","reasoning_cat2":"It is the input to almost every distribution formula and to the Overcollateralization definitions; no inconsistency found.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.10},

{"clause_id":"c340","reasoning_cat1":"A five-branch rate definition with a June 2008 switch and a 10.440% cap; long but each branch is spelled out, and the '2 multiplied by' leverage is stated.","reasoning_cat2":"It is the input to the Uncertificated REMIC II Pass-Through Rate table and the Marker Rate; consistent in structure.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.15},

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c358","reasoning_cat1":"The closing sentence — 'shall be the sole remedies respecting such defect available to the Certificateholders or to the Securities Administrator on their behalf' — is a sole-remedy limitation that mixes singular obligation with plural 'remedies' and is confined to 'a defect in a constituent document', leaving open whether it reaches representation-and-warranty breaches.","reasoning_cat2":"It names only the Certificateholders and the Securities Administrator, yet Section 2.02(d) directs the Trustee to enforce repurchase, cure and substitution obligations 'on behalf of the Trust', so the sole-remedy limitation and the Trustee's enforcement mandate pull in different directions.","prob_cat1":0.50,"prob_cat2":0.53},
{"clause_id":"c359","reasoning_cat1":"The Trustee's duty extends to 'any other obligations of the related Seller or the related Originator under such agreements' — an unbounded catch-all after specific repurchase/cure/substitute duties — and the Accredited backstop is expressed as an 'including, without limitation' example rather than a separate covenant.","reasoning_cat2":"It sits directly against Section 2.02(c)'s sole-remedy sentence and against Section 2.03's repurchase paragraphs, and the obligations it tells the Trustee to enforce live in the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement and Bring Down Agreements rather than in this instrument.","prob_cat1":0.47,"prob_cat2":0.50},
{"clause_id":"c360","reasoning_cat1":"The section is captioned as the Master Servicer's and Securities Administrator's representations and its lettered clauses are Wells Fargo's own corporate representations, yet the unlettered paragraphs that follow impose notice, substitution and repurchase machinery on Sellers and Originators who make no representations here at all.","reasoning_cat2":"Numerous other provisions — the Mortgage Loans definition (Section 2.03(b)(v)), Substitution Adjustment Amount (Section 2.03(d)), Replacement Mortgage Loan condition (ix), Sections 2.05(a), 2.05(b), 4.02 and the Interest Funds and Principal Funds definitions — treat Section 2.03 as the source of loan-level representations and remedies, which it is not.","prob_cat1":0.45,"prob_cat2":0.58},
{"clause_id":"c361","reasoning_cat1":"A one-sentence survival clause; its oddity is that it makes representations survive 'delivery of the respective Mortgage Loans and Mortgage Files', language apt for loan-level warranties.","reasoning_cat2":"The representations 'set forth in Section 2.03' are Wells Fargo's corporate representations, which have nothing to do with delivery of Mortgage Files, and the Mortgage Loans definition cites a non-existent Section 2.03(b)(v) as if this subsection contained loan-level warranties.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.49},
{"clause_id":"c362","reasoning_cat1":"'Upon discovery by the Depositor, the Trustee of a breach' is missing a conjunction, clause (ii) is mislabelled 'Gi)', and the title representation is squeezed into an unnumbered paragraph after the enumerated corporate representations.","reasoning_cat2":"The Depositor's good-title representation survives delivery and triggers a notice duty, but no cure, repurchase or substitution remedy is provided for its breach anywhere in the Agreement, unlike the Seller and Originator representations addressed by Sections 2.02(c)–(d).","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.33},
{"clause_id":"c363","reasoning_cat1":"'not in default or as to which default is not reasonably foreseeable' is a forward-looking, contestable standard, and the REMIC list is garbled ('REMIC I, REMIC I').","reasoning_cat2":"It conditions repurchases and substitutions 'pursuant to Sections 2.02 or 2.03', but Section 2.03 as drafted contains no loan-level representations to be breached, so the trigger it assumes is not there.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c364","reasoning_cat1":"The remedy is expressed as being 'at such party's option' among cure, substitution or repurchase, while also imposing a 90-day outer limit only on limb (iii), and 'the same manner as it would a Mortgage Loan subject to repurchase' is an elliptical construction.","reasoning_cat2":"It has the Securities Administrator or Custodian reconvey the loan, whereas Sections 2.02(c) and 2.03 have the Trustee or Custodian release the Mortgage File and execute the transfer instruments — different actors for the same step.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.34},
{"clause_id":"c365","reasoning_cat1":"Short acknowledgment and undertaking; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 2.01's conveyance and the Trustee definition; the statement that the Certificates evidence 'the entire ownership of the Trust Fund' sits alongside the Supplemental Interest Trust exclusions but does not conflict with them.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c366","reasoning_cat1":"Definite conveyance and acknowledgment, with only OCR-level slips ('REMIC IT').","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Preliminary Statement's REMIC II paragraph and the REMIC I Regular Interest definition.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c367","reasoning_cat1":"Definite conveyance with a carefully enumerated beneficiary list.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Preliminary Statement's REMIC III paragraph and the Class CE/P/IO Interest definitions.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c368","reasoning_cat1":"Definite conveyance; parallel structure to (c) and (e).","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the REMIC IV and Class CE Interest definitions.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c369","reasoning_cat1":"Definite conveyance; parallel structure.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the REMIC V and Class P Interest definitions.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c370","reasoning_cat1":"Definite conveyance; parallel structure.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the REMIC VI and Class IO Interest definitions and the Supplemental Interest Trust definition, which holds REMIC VI Regular Interest IO.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c371","reasoning_cat1":"Limb (a) omits the infinitive 'to' that every other limb has, limb (d) is an open-ended 'necessary, suitable or convenient ... or incidental thereto' catch-all, and the section ends with the dangling fragment 'and this Section 2.07.'","reasoning_cat2":"The purposes list must accommodate Section 4.22's Supplemental Interest Trust and swap arrangements, which are not obviously within limbs (a) to (c) and depend on the breadth of the catch-alls.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.21},
{"clause_id":"c372","reasoning_cat1":"A very long provision mixing an absolute duty ('shall cause the Servicers to perform and observe the covenants') with broad discretion ('full power and authority to do any and all things which it may deem necessary or desirable'), and the reconciliation sentence refers back to 'the previous sentence' loosely.","reasoning_cat2":"The absolute 'shall cause the Servicers to perform' duty here is measured in Section 4.03(b) by a much softer standard ('as the Master Servicer in its good faith business judgment would require were it the owner'), so the two sections state the same duty differently.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c373","reasoning_cat1":"Definite three-limb prohibition with REMIC Opinion exceptions; the REMIC list contains the usual 'REMIC I, REMIC I' slip.","reasoning_cat2":"It requires the Trustee to 'comply with any directions of the Seller, the Servicers or the Master Servicer', which sits awkwardly with the Trustee's independent duties in Article X, and it treats Section 2.03 as a source of substitutions.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c374","reasoning_cat1":"'in its judgment' and 'take such other action as it deems appropriate' leave the Master Servicer's obligation almost entirely discretionary despite the mandatory 'shall be responsible for reporting'.","reasoning_cat2":"The carve-out '(other than Wells Fargo)' is picked up and completed by Section 4.03(b), which routes Wells Fargo's termination through the Trustee; the two subsections fit.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c375","reasoning_cat1":"The final sentence is a double negative that is hard to apply ('Nothing herein shall impose any obligation on the part of the Trustee to assume ... unless the Trustee has not been able to find a successor servicer'), and 'Successor master Servicer' is used with irregular capitalisation for a term defined elsewhere.","reasoning_cat2":"The enforcement standard here ('as it would were it the owner of the related Mortgage Loans') is softer than the absolute duty to 'cause the Servicers to perform' in Section 4.01, and the last sentence potentially obliges the Trustee to assume master servicing, which Section 8.06 governs.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c376","reasoning_cat1":"Long but carefully itemised reimbursement provision; 'Successor Servicer' is capitalised here though the Agreement uses 'successor servicer' elsewhere.","reasoning_cat2":"Reimbursement 'from the Distribution Account' must be squared with Sections 5.02 and 5.03, which govern permitted withdrawals from that account.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c377","reasoning_cat1":"A one-sentence obligation; definite, if bare.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 4.01 and 4.03(b) and the Remittance Date definition.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c378","reasoning_cat1":"'the representations and warranties of the related Servicer, if any' leaves it unstated whether any such representations exist and where they are found.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 4.03(b)'s provision for the Master Servicer to act as servicer on termination; no conflict found.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c379","reasoning_cat1":"The bond and policy must be 'in such form and amount generally acceptable for entities serving as master servicers or trustees' — a wholly external and unquantified standard with no minimum coverage stated.","reasoning_cat2":"No other provision fixes coverage amounts or gives another party approval rights, so the standard has no anchor elsewhere in the instrument.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c380","reasoning_cat1":"A long grant of 'full power and authority to do any and all things that it may deem necessary or desirable', qualified by a REMIC proviso; the REMIC lists are garbled ('REMIC J', 'REMIC II, REMIC II') and the parenthetical '(and the Trustee shall have no liability for misuse ... by the Master Servicer, the related Servicer)' omits a conjunction.","reasoning_cat2":"The breadth of the discretion has to be read against Section 4.01's Accepted Master Servicing Practices standard and Article XI, and the co-trustee mechanism points to Section 10.11.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c381","reasoning_cat1":"The operative content is almost entirely circular — enforcement and release of the Mortgagor are each 'in accordance with this Agreement or the related Servicing Agreement' — so the section states no independent rule, and 'may be released' is permissive without saying who decides.","reasoning_cat2":"The substance is left to the Servicing Agreements, which are external documents; nothing in this Agreement fills the gap.","prob_cat1":0.25,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c382","reasoning_cat1":"Long but procedurally specific; the parenthetical '(or if the related Servicer does not, the Master Servicer may)' makes the backstop permissive rather than mandatory.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Request for Release definition and Exhibit G, and with the Protected Account provisions in Section 5.01.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c383","reasoning_cat1":"The sentence 'Such trust receipt shall obligate the related Servicer or the Master Servicer to return the Mortgage File' refers to a 'trust receipt' that is never mentioned earlier in the subsection — a dangling antecedent left over from a form.","reasoning_cat2":"The preceding sentence provides only for a 'request for release' in the form of Exhibit G, so the obligation to return the file is attached to a document this Agreement does not create.","prob_cat1":0.32,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c384","reasoning_cat1":"The access sentence is garbled — 'The Master Servicer, the related Servicer shall provide access to information and documentation regarding the Mortgage Loans to the Trustee and, regarding the Mortgage Loans and their respective agents and accountants' — so it cannot be read as written.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 4.01 contains a parallel and differently worded access provision covering Certificateholders and the FDIC, and this one adds the OTS and other regulators, leaving two overlapping access regimes.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c385","reasoning_cat1":"'the Master Servicer, the related Servicer shall be entitled to setoff' omits a conjunction, and the funds are said to 'be and remain the sole and exclusive property of the Trustee' while simultaneously being subject to setoff.","reasoning_cat2":"The setoff right must be reconciled with Section 4.08(a) and with Sections 5.01 and 5.03, which specify permitted withdrawals and reimbursements.","prob_cat1":0.25,"prob_cat2":0.21},
{"clause_id":"c386","reasoning_cat1":"Definite in substance; the duty is to enforce the Servicers' insurance obligations rather than to insure, and the no-earthquake-insurance sentence is clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Insurance Policy definition and Section 4.10.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c387","reasoning_cat1":"The provision opens 'Pursuant to Sections 5.01 and 5.04' and then permits withdrawal 'pursuant to Sections 5.02, 5.03 or 5.04' and recovery 'pursuant to Sections 5.01 or 5.03' — three different citation sets for one flow of funds.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 5.04 is the Yield Maintenance Credit Support Annex provision and Section 5.02 is the Distribution Account, so the citations do not match Article V as drafted.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.35},
{"clause_id":"c388","reasoning_cat1":"Definite; the exception for restoration amounts is expressed as a condition precedent and is workable.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Insurance Proceeds and Insured Expenses definitions and Section 4.09(b).","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.12}
]}

{"clause_id":"c364","reasoning_cat1":"The remedy is expressed as being 'at such party's option' among cure, substitution or repurchase, while also imposing a 90-day outer limit only on limb (iii), and 'the same manner as it would a Mortgage Loan subject to repurchase' is an elliptical construction.","reasoning_cat2":"It has the Securities Administrator or Custodian reconvey the loan, whereas Sections 2.02(c) and 2.03 have the Trustee or Custodian release the Mortgage File and execute the transfer instruments — different actors for the same step.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.34},
{"clause_id":"c365","reasoning_cat1":"Short acknowledgment and undertaking; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 2.01's conveyance and the Trustee definition; the statement that the Certificates evidence 'the entire ownership of the Trust Fund' sits alongside the Supplemental Interest Trust exclusions but does not conflict with them.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c366","reasoning_cat1":"Definite conveyance and acknowledgment, with only OCR-level slips ('REMIC IT').","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Preliminary Statement's REMIC II paragraph and the REMIC I Regular Interest definition.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c367","reasoning_cat1":"Definite conveyance with a carefully enumerated beneficiary list.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Preliminary Statement's REMIC III paragraph and the Class CE/P/IO Interest definitions.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c368","reasoning_cat1":"Definite conveyance; parallel structure to (c) and (e).","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the REMIC IV and Class CE Interest definitions.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c369","reasoning_cat1":"Definite conveyance; parallel structure.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the REMIC V and Class P Interest definitions.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c370","reasoning_cat1":"Definite conveyance; parallel structure.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the REMIC VI and Class IO Interest definitions and the Supplemental Interest Trust definition, which holds REMIC VI Regular Interest IO.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c371","reasoning_cat1":"Limb (a) omits the infinitive 'to' that every other limb has, limb (d) is an open-ended 'necessary, suitable or convenient ... or incidental thereto' catch-all, and the section ends with the dangling fragment 'and this Section 2.07.'","reasoning_cat2":"The purposes list must accommodate Section 4.22's Supplemental Interest Trust and swap arrangements, which are not obviously within limbs (a) to (c) and depend on the breadth of the catch-alls.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.21},
{"clause_id":"c372","reasoning_cat1":"A very long provision mixing an absolute duty ('shall cause the Servicers to perform and observe the covenants') with broad discretion ('full power and authority to do any and all things which it may deem necessary or desirable'), and the reconciliation sentence refers back to 'the previous sentence' loosely.","reasoning_cat2":"The absolute 'shall cause the Servicers to perform' duty here is measured in Section 4.03(b) by a much softer standard ('as the Master Servicer in its good faith business judgment would require were it the owner'), so the two sections state the same duty differently.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c373","reasoning_cat1":"Definite three-limb prohibition with REMIC Opinion exceptions; the REMIC list contains the usual 'REMIC I, REMIC I' slip.","reasoning_cat2":"It requires the Trustee to 'comply with any directions of the Seller, the Servicers or the Master Servicer', which sits awkwardly with the Trustee's independent duties in Article X, and it treats Section 2.03 as a source of substitutions.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c374","reasoning_cat1":"'in its judgment' and 'take such other action as it deems appropriate' leave the Master Servicer's obligation almost entirely discretionary despite the mandatory 'shall be responsible for reporting'.","reasoning_cat2":"The carve-out '(other than Wells Fargo)' is picked up and completed by Section 4.03(b), which routes Wells Fargo's termination through the Trustee; the two subsections fit.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c375","reasoning_cat1":"The final sentence is a double negative that is hard to apply ('Nothing herein shall impose any obligation on the part of the Trustee to assume ... unless the Trustee has not been able to find a successor servicer'), and 'Successor master Servicer' is used with irregular capitalisation for a term defined elsewhere.","reasoning_cat2":"The enforcement standard here ('as it would were it the owner of the related Mortgage Loans') is softer than the absolute duty to 'cause the Servicers to perform' in Section 4.01, and the last sentence potentially obliges the Trustee to assume master servicing, which Section 8.06 governs.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c376","reasoning_cat1":"Long but carefully itemised reimbursement provision; 'Successor Servicer' is capitalised here though the Agreement uses 'successor servicer' elsewhere.","reasoning_cat2":"Reimbursement 'from the Distribution Account' must be squared with Sections 5.02 and 5.03, which govern permitted withdrawals from that account.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c377","reasoning_cat1":"A one-sentence obligation; definite, if bare.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 4.01 and 4.03(b) and the Remittance Date definition.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c378","reasoning_cat1":"'the representations and warranties of the related Servicer, if any' leaves it unstated whether any such representations exist and where they are found.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 4.03(b)'s provision for the Master Servicer to act as servicer on termination; no conflict found.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c379","reasoning_cat1":"The bond and policy must be 'in such form and amount generally acceptable for entities serving as master servicers or trustees' — a wholly external and unquantified standard with no minimum coverage stated.","reasoning_cat2":"No other provision fixes coverage amounts or gives another party approval rights, so the standard has no anchor elsewhere in the instrument.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c380","reasoning_cat1":"A long grant of 'full power and authority to do any and all things that it may deem necessary or desirable', qualified by a REMIC proviso; the REMIC lists are garbled ('REMIC J', 'REMIC II, REMIC II') and the parenthetical '(and the Trustee shall have no liability for misuse ... by the Master Servicer, the related Servicer)' omits a conjunction.","reasoning_cat2":"The breadth of the discretion has to be read against Section 4.01's Accepted Master Servicing Practices standard and Article XI, and the co-trustee mechanism points to Section 10.11.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c381","reasoning_cat1":"The operative content is almost entirely circular — enforcement and release of the Mortgagor are each 'in accordance with this Agreement or the related Servicing Agreement' — so the section states no independent rule, and 'may be released' is permissive without saying who decides.","reasoning_cat2":"The substance is left to the Servicing Agreements, which are external documents; nothing in this Agreement fills the gap.","prob_cat1":0.25,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c382","reasoning_cat1":"Long but procedurally specific; the parenthetical '(or if the related Servicer does not, the Master Servicer may)' makes the backstop permissive rather than mandatory.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Request for Release definition and Exhibit G, and with the Protected Account provisions in Section 5.01.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c383","reasoning_cat1":"The sentence 'Such trust receipt shall obligate the related Servicer or the Master Servicer to return the Mortgage File' refers to a 'trust receipt' that is never mentioned earlier in the subsection — a dangling antecedent left over from a form.","reasoning_cat2":"The preceding sentence provides only for a 'request for release' in the form of Exhibit G, so the obligation to return the file is attached to a document this Agreement does not create.","prob_cat1":0.32,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c384","reasoning_cat1":"The access sentence is garbled — 'The Master Servicer, the related Servicer shall provide access to information and documentation regarding the Mortgage Loans to the Trustee and, regarding the Mortgage Loans and their respective agents and accountants' — so it cannot be read as written.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 4.01 contains a parallel and differently worded access provision covering Certificateholders and the FDIC, and this one adds the OTS and other regulators, leaving two overlapping access regimes.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c385","reasoning_cat1":"'the Master Servicer, the related Servicer shall be entitled to setoff' omits a conjunction, and the funds are said to 'be and remain the sole and exclusive property of the Trustee' while simultaneously being subject to setoff.","reasoning_cat2":"The setoff right must be reconciled with Section 4.08(a) and with Sections 5.01 and 5.03, which specify permitted withdrawals and reimbursements.","prob_cat1":0.25,"prob_cat2":0.21},
{"clause_id":"c386","reasoning_cat1":"Definite in substance; the duty is to enforce the Servicers' insurance obligations rather than to insure, and the no-earthquake-insurance sentence is clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Insurance Policy definition and Section 4.10.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c387","reasoning_cat1":"The provision opens 'Pursuant to Sections 5.01 and 5.04' and then permits withdrawal 'pursuant to Sections 5.02, 5.03 or 5.04' and recovery 'pursuant to Sections 5.01 or 5.03' — three different citation sets for one flow of funds.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 5.04 is the Yield Maintenance Credit Support Annex provision and Section 5.02 is the Distribution Account, so the citations do not match Article V as drafted.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.35},
{"clause_id":"c388","reasoning_cat1":"Definite; the exception for restoration amounts is expressed as a condition precedent and is workable.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Insurance Proceeds and Insured Expenses definitions and Section 4.09(b).","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.12}
]}

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c389","reasoning_cat1":"'use its best reasonable efforts' blends two different legal standards, and the phrase 'but for the actions of the Master Servicer, the related Servicer' omits a conjunction.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Primary Mortgage Insurance Policy and LPMI Policy definitions, though the coverage period in the former definition is garbled.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.18},
{"clause_id":"c390","reasoning_cat1":"The provision opens 'Pursuant to Sections 5.01 and 5.05' and permits withdrawal 'pursuant to Section 5.02'.","reasoning_cat2":"Article V of this Agreement runs only from Section 5.01 to Section 5.04, so 'Section 5.05' names a provision that does not exist.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.38},
{"clause_id":"c391","reasoning_cat1":"The heading says the Trustee is to retain possession, while the text places possession and custody in the Custodians on the Trustee's behalf — heading and operative text do not match.","reasoning_cat2":"The Custodial Agreements and Section 2.01's delivery-to-Custodian sentence support the text rather than the heading, so the mismatch is formal but real.","prob_cat1":0.23,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c392","reasoning_cat1":"'as to which no satisfactory arrangements can be made for collection of delinquent payments' is an unmeasured standard, and the operative content is then wholly deferred to 'this Agreement or the related Servicing Agreement'.","reasoning_cat2":"The substantive foreclosure standards live in the Servicing Agreements, which are external documents; nothing in this Agreement supplies them.","prob_cat1":0.23,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c393","reasoning_cat1":"Definite in structure: fee, float income, expense-bearing and a Compensating Interest offset.","reasoning_cat2":"The float income is granted here and is also built into both the Master Servicing Fee and Master Servicing Compensation definitions, so the same entitlement is stated three times in different words with a risk of double counting.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c394","reasoning_cat1":"'sell, any REO Property as expeditiously as possible' contains a stray comma and an unmeasured urgency standard, and 'protect and conserve, such REO Property' repeats the error.","reasoning_cat2":"The REMIC 'foreclosure property' constraint referenced here has to be read with Section 4.02 and the REO Property definition, which attributes acquisition to the Servicer rather than the Trust Fund.","prob_cat1":0.20,"prob_cat2":0.18},
{"clause_id":"c395","reasoning_cat1":"A single short sentence; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Protected Account definition and Section 5.01.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c396","reasoning_cat1":"The proviso refers to 'any such unreimbursed Monthly Advances', a term this Agreement never defines and which does not correspond to the 'Advances' used in the preceding clause.","reasoning_cat2":"Article I defines 'Advance' and 'Servicing Advances' but not 'Monthly Advances', so the proviso's referent has to be supplied from outside the instrument.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.25},
{"clause_id":"c397","reasoning_cat1":"'the related Distribution Account' uses the definite article for an account of which there is only one, and the sentence lacks a comma before 'shall be deposited'.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Liquidation Proceeds, Protected Account and Remittance Date definitions.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c398","reasoning_cat1":"The section deems non-compliance an 'Event of Default' and then declares 'This paragraph shall supersede any other provision in this Agreement or any other agreement to the contrary' — a sweeping override embedded in a reporting covenant, with an immediate termination remedy and no cure period.","reasoning_cat2":"Event of Default is defined by reference to Section 9.01, and Article IX contains its own notice and cure machinery for terminating the Master Servicer, so this deeming-plus-supersession paragraph cannot be harmonised with that regime.","prob_cat1":0.32,"prob_cat2":0.44},
{"clause_id":"c399","reasoning_cat1":"Very long and detailed; its notable feature is the same 'This paragraph shall supersede any other provision in this Agreement or any other agreement to the contrary' override coupled with immediate termination for a reporting failure.","reasoning_cat2":"It again deems a reporting failure an Event of Default outside Section 9.01's definition and cure structure, and it treats the Securities Administrator's failure as a 'default' rather than an Event of Default, a distinction the Agreement does not otherwise draw.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.41},
{"clause_id":"c400","reasoning_cat1":"Extremely long and procedurally dense, and it twice directs the reader to 'Section 4.18(a)(vi)(B)' for late or amended filings when the late-filing procedure is in Section 4.18(a)(v)(B) and no subsection (vi) appears.","reasoning_cat2":"The mis-numbered cross-reference points outside the subsections that Section 4.18(a) actually contains, and the liability carve-out here must be read with the indemnities in Section 4.18(b).","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.34},
